summary: Adversarial review of the pose-sequence action classifier before its held-out measurement

issues.issue: The reported mlp_sum@FA1 numbers come from one lucky torch seed. The threshold is set by about 5 normal-video events, so it jumps from seed to seed, and recall jumps with it.
issues.evidence: I re-ran the module's own CV with exp/actions/review_tmp/cv.py. Seed 0 reproduces the report exactly: thr 0.786, alone 89.1/73.5, add-on 97.0/87.0, FA 0.98 and 6.07. Seed 1 gives thr 0.888, alone 77.0/57.8, add-on 93.5/79.6. Seed 2 gives thr 0.804, alone 88.3/74.3, add-on 96.5/84.8. Video-grouped folds over seeds 0-2 give add-on crop 80.0, 79.6 and 83.0, and alone crop 64.8, 61.7 and 71.3. The OOF AUC barely moves (0.76-0.78), so the swing comes from the threshold. The reported 87.0 add-on crop and 73.5 alone crop are the top of the range. The choice of mlp_sum@1.0 out of 6 variants x 4 targets on the same OOF scores adds more selection optimism.
issues.fix: Before the held-out run, report tune numbers as a range over 3 or more seeds and over video-grouped folds: add-on littering crop about 80-87 (mean about 82), alone crop about 58-74. A sturdier option is to freeze a seed-averaged ensemble, with the threshold calibrated on the averaged OOF scores. State that the held-out result is a single draw of the seed-0 model.

issues.issue: Every held-out littering clip comes from a source video that also has clips in the tune half. The full model that will score held-out was trained on all 230 tune clips. So held-out littering does not test the learned cue on unseen actors or scenes.
issues.evidence: This uses metadata only (data/littering/clips.csv, columns class+video+split); no held-out frames or caches were loaded. All 100 valid+test clips share a source video with train clips (52 of 52 held-out videos). No clip_id appears in both halves, so there are no cache-key collisions. The montage of dropping_v01_2 and v01_4 shows the same two actors in the same scene.
issues.fix: State this plainly in the held-out report. Tune evidence suggests the effect is modest: video-grouped CV had OOF AUC 0.774-0.780 vs 0.760-0.766 clip-grouped, with no drop. Still, frame the held-out littering number as 'same videos, new clips'. Avenue/normal/smoking held-out are on genuinely unseen videos or days and are the cleaner generalization test.

issues.issue: The FA threshold is in-sample on a tiny set. Tune normal footage is 5.1 min, and the reported 0.98 FA/min is exactly 5 events, 3 of them from train/01. On average the calibration is not biased, but its error bar is about as large as the target itself.
issues.evidence: exp/actions/review_tmp/calib.py on the module's own OOF scores. Over all 70 4-vs-4 splits of the 8 normal videos (calibrate on one half, measure on the other): mean FA 0.86, median 0.5, p10 0.0, p90 2.08. 33% of splits exceed 1/min and 11% exceed 2/min, with thr 0.761-0.927. Leave-one-video-out calibration gives a pooled FA of 0.98, with per-video FA from 0 to 4.1/min.
issues.fix: Report normal FA as about 1/min with a split-half spread of 0-2/min, not as 0.98. The add-on's '+1 FA/min over baseline' is uncertain by about ±1/min. If possible, calibrate on more normal minutes (all tune normal windows are already used, so this needs more footage).

issues.issue: Held-out scoring uses the full model with a threshold calibrated on fold-model OOF scores, so the tune numbers come from a different model-plus-threshold combination than the one that will run on held-out. A nested simulation of that exact procedure gives clearly lower recall.
issues.evidence: Nested video-grouped simulation (outer fold aside; inner 4-fold OOF calibrates thr; outer 'full' model trained on the rest scores the outer normal and littering data), seeds 0-2: outer FA 0.20, 0.20 and 0.59; alone crop 51.7, 41.3 and 55.7; add-on event/crop 90.4/74.3, 87.4/70.4 and 92.6/78.7. Part of the drop comes from training on less data, so treat this as a pessimistic bound. For the real full model, the score scale shift is small: on tune Avenue, 1.03% of windows exceed thr under the full model vs 0.63-0.99% under the fold models.
issues.fix: Quote the nested figures (add-on crop about 70-79, FA increment about 0.2-0.6/min) as the lower end of the tune estimate, so the one-time held-out result is read against a realistic range, not against 87.0.

issues.issue: Live-path model loading needs `pose_seq` importable as a top-level module, because the pickles reference pose_seq.TorchModel. Importing the module under a package path or by file location makes every unseen sequence fail.
issues.evidence: exp/actions/review_tmp/c5.py, imported via spec_from_file_location('exp.actions.pose_seq'), raises ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pose_seq' on the live path. With exp/actions on sys.path, the live path matches the cached path exactly for an Avenue sequence. The failure is loud, not silent.
issues.fix: In the held-out runner, put /Users/ianvarella/capstone_S25/notebooks/exp/actions on sys.path and `import pose_seq`. This needs no module change. Assert that every held-out seq_id goes through the live path.

issues.issue: The docstring and report say the folds are 'clip-grouped', and that is literally what they are. But all 60 tune source videos have clips in more than one fold, so sibling clips with the same actors sit in training for every OOF score.
issues.evidence: exp/actions/review_tmp/c2.py: 60 source videos, all 60 span more than 1 fold. In practice this did not inflate the tune numbers (see the AUC comparison above).
issues.fix: Say 'grouped by clip, not by source video', or switch build() folds to group by class_vNN in a future rebuild. Do not rebuild before the held-out run unless every reported number is regenerated.

result.summary:
Audit verdict: the code is honest, but the headline tune numbers are optimistic and must be reported as ranges before the one-time held-out run.

Checks that passed:
- (1) Inference is causal and never reads ground truth. 64 truncation checks found 0 mismatches. The method only sees result objects (observations and rule events), and labels are used only in build().
- (2) Every tune littering clip and normal video is scored out-of-fold. Seed 0 reproduces the report exactly. Avenue and smoking are scored by the full model, which never trained on them. Cached Avenue scores match a fresh predict from model_mlp_sum.pkl.
- (4) The module never retrains or touches held-out data. Unseen seq_ids take the live path with the pickled full model, and no held-out clip_id collides with a tune cache key.

Problems found:
- Seed and threshold sensitivity: the threshold rests on 5 events in 5.1 normal minutes. Add-on littering crop ranges 79.6-87.0 across seeds (alone 57.8-74.3), and the reported 87.0/73.5 is the best draw.
- FA calibration: split-half calibration is unbiased on average (mean 0.86, median 0.5/min) but very noisy (p90 2.08; a third of the splits exceed the 1/min target).
- Nested simulation of the actual held-out procedure (full model plus OOF threshold) gives add-on crop 70-79 and alone crop 41-56. This is a pessimistic bound.
- All 100 held-out littering clips share source videos (actors and scenes) with tune clips the full model trained on. Video-grouped tune CV showed no AUC loss, so the effect is probably small, but it must be disclosed.
- Loading the model by package path fails with ModuleNotFoundError, so exp/actions must be on sys.path in the held-out runner.

Scratch scripts and outputs are in /Users/ianvarella/capstone_S25/notebooks/exp/actions/review_tmp/ (cv.py, calib.py, c4.py, c5.py, cv_compare.json, calib.json).

issues.issue: The headline add-on number (littering 87.0% crop) comes from a lucky seed. The 1 FA/min threshold is set from about 5 events in 5.1 minutes of normal video, so it jumps between seeds and the candidate rate jumps with it.
issues.evidence: I retrained mlp_sum with the same folds and weights. Seed 0 reproduces the cache exactly (thr 0.786). Across seeds 0/1/2/3: thr 0.786/0.888/0.804/0.897; candidates per clip 1.39/1.05/1.37/1.05; crop alone 73.5/57.8/74.3/57.0; add-on littering crop 87.0/79.6/84.8/79.6 (mean about 82.8). The ranking itself is stable: within-clip AUC 0.747-0.762, and skill over tallest-at-same-times is +10.8 to +15.2 in every seed. The instability is in the threshold.
issues.fix: Before the held-out run, fix the model to an ensemble or average of 3-5 seeds and fix the threshold, preferably calibrated on more normal minutes. Report the tune numbers as mean and spread over seeds (add-on about 80-87, alone about 57-74), not the single 87.0/73.5.

issues.issue: Most of the add-on's littering gain comes from roughly doubling the number of candidates on the littering camera, not from better selection.
issues.evidence: Baseline gives 1.43 candidates per clip and 16.6 non-hit candidates per minute on the littering clips. Add-on gives 2.82 per clip and 29.1 non-hit per minute. Crop recall rises 55.7 to 87.0, but the rate-matched distinct-person lift only goes from +10.3 to +13.1. On Avenue test, non-hit candidates rise from 4.92 to 6.63 per minute.
issues.fix: State the add-on result as 'about 2x VLM candidates on close-up cameras for +31 crop points, of which about +3 is above rate-matched random'. Judge it against a VLM candidate budget, not only the normal-video FA figure.

issues.issue: The model has partly learned the camera. The Avenue-calibrated threshold does not carry over, and calibrating on the littering camera removes most of the gain.
issues.evidence: Frame sizes: littering is 1080x1920; normal and Avenue are 360x640; smoking is 480x640. A logistic probe on the same summary features separates littering windows from normal ones with grouped-CV AUC 0.982. Share of windows above the threshold: littering bystanders 19.1%, normal 0.36% (about 53x), Avenue test 1.03%, smoking 8.26%. mlp scores of littering bystanders vs normal people: AUC 0.832. A threshold calibrated in-sample to 1 bystander candidate per minute on the littering camera (thr 0.986) gives crop 6.1% alone and add-on 57.8% (baseline 55.7). At 4 per minute it gives 20.9% alone and add-on 63.0%.
issues.fix: Require per-camera threshold calibration on that camera's own normal footage before deployment, and do not quote 1 FA/min as a deployment figure. Ideally add normal negatives from a 1080p close-up camera, or train with camera-balanced negatives, so the negatives stop acting as a camera label.

issues.issue: Part of the person-choice skill is a size or closeness prior. The remaining skill is real but depends on the action: it is strong for tossing and dropping and missing for putting-down and throwing.
issues.evidence: At the mlp's own fire times and counts, picking the person crops: mlp 73.5, tallest 60.0, largest area 57.4, distinct random 55.9. Size explains about 4 of the 17.6-point lift. Per action (mlp / tallest / random): dropping 67.4/52.2/52.4; dumping 80.4/67.4/63.7; putting-down 69.6/63.0/61.1; throwing 80.4/69.6/44.4; tossing 69.6/47.8/58.0. Within-clip AUC vs box height: throwing 0.829 vs 0.877 (size wins); tossing 0.670 vs 0.466. Top-1 accuracy at contested moments: overall mlp 53.2, tallest 48.7, chance 41.3; putting-down mlp 44.1, below chance at 46.1. When the bystander is taller, mlp ranks the actor higher in only 59.4% of 357 pairs.
issues.fix: Report skill over tallest-at-same-times (+13.5 on seed 0) as the honest action-skill number, broken down by action. Make no action-skill claim for throwing or putting-down.

issues.issue: The 'tallest person in frame' reference in diagnose() is not rate-matched or time-matched, so it is a weak comparison.
issues.evidence: diagnose() tallest fires at 1.19 candidates per clip, at its own times, with 19.6 normal FA per minute. mlp fires at 1.39 per clip. The same-times tallest control above gives 60.0 vs 73.5.
issues.fix: Replace it with the same-times, same-count tallest control. The script is /Users/ianvarella/capstone_S25/notebooks/exp/actions/review_tmp/skeptic.py, function same_time.

issues.issue: The normal-video FA rate is in-sample for the threshold and optimistic even on the same camera.
issues.evidence: mlp non-hit candidates per minute: 0.98 on tune normal (the calibration set) vs 1.70 on Avenue tune test videos (same camera, not used for calibration). Smoking camera: 1.76 per minute.
issues.fix: Quote about 1.7 per minute as the same-camera estimate. Expect the held-out normal FA to come in above 1.0.

issues.issue: Adding the normal negatives lowered within-clip actor-vs-bystander skill. They mainly teach the model to tell the cameras apart.
issues.evidence: Within-clip AUC: lr_sum_lit 0.771 and mlp_sum_lit 0.756 vs mlp_sum 0.747. The author's what_failed item 2 says the same.
issues.fix: Note this in the report. If time allows, try a two-part score (a littering-only actor model times a per-camera normalised gate) instead of mixing the cameras in one training set.

result.summary:
Recommendation: adopt with caveats, and only as an experimental add-on, not with the claimed numbers. I assumed the computations are correct and checked whether the gain is real action skill on the tune half only (YOLO26s cache, nothing held-out loaded). Seed 0 reproduces the cached results exactly.

(a) Size prior. At the mlp's own fire times and counts, picking the tallest person gets 60.0% crop, distinct random gets 55.9%, and mlp gets 73.5%. Size explains about 4 of the 17.6-point person-choice lift, and about +13.5 is beyond size. That remainder holds across seeds (+10.8 to +15.2). It is strong for tossing, dropping and dumping. For throwing the size prior is better than the model (within-clip AUC 0.877 vs 0.829), and for putting-down the model is at or below chance (contested-moment top-1 44.1% vs 46.1% chance).

(b) Camera. Within littering clips the model still separates actor from bystander better than size: within-clip AUC 0.747 vs 0.707, and it wins 59% of pairs where the bystander is taller. So it is not purely camera. But the features identify the camera almost perfectly (probe AUC 0.982). 19% of littering-bystander windows pass the threshold against 0.36% of normal windows.

(c) Deployment. On the 1080p camera the add-on doubles candidates (1.43 to 2.82 per clip; non-hit candidates 16.6 to 29.1 per minute). The rate-matched lift only moves from +10.3 to +13.1. Calibrating the threshold in-sample to 1 bystander candidate per minute on that camera shrinks the add-on gain to +2.1 points (+7.3 at 4 per minute). Even on the same Avenue camera, videos outside the calibration set show 1.7 non-hit per minute, not 0.98. A deployment needs per-camera normal footage for calibration and a candidate budget for the VLM.

(d) Seeds. The ranking is stable, but the threshold (set from about 5 events in 5.1 minutes) is not. Across 4 seeds the add-on gives 79.6 to 87.0 littering crop (mean about 82.8) and alone gives 57.0 to 74.3, so the reported 87.0/73.5 is the high end. Before the one-time held-out run: fix a seed ensemble and threshold, report tune results as mean and spread over seeds, and quote skill over tallest-at-same-times per action as the action-skill number.

Scripts and results: /Users/ianvarella/capstone_S25/notebooks/exp/actions/review_tmp/skeptic.py, /Users/ianvarella/capstone_S25/notebooks/exp/actions/review_tmp/extra.py, /Users/ianvarella/capstone_S25/notebooks/exp/actions/review_tmp/skeptic.json.
